title: Wendell and the Hollow
premise: Paloma Sterling has spent her life guarding the Hollow Gate, the last seal on a country that was unmade a century ago and whose old gods have been silent ever since. When prayers begin to be answered again — first hers, then a stranger's — she learns the gate is failing and that the vanished nation of Vessany is bleeding back into the world through her valley. Guided by Wendell, a memory-keeper who remembers Vessany better than its own ghosts do, Paloma must find the true door out of a country that no longer exists before the moon completes its thirteenth turn and the gate opens for good. In the end, Paloma chooses justice over law: she does not shut the door but becomes it, letting Vessany's people choose their own return while Wendell's loyalty forces him to surrender the truth he kept from her.
about_author: Isandro Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records from regions redrawn by treaty. They write fantasy about places erased from maps and the people who refuse to forget them.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Prayers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She tends the Hollow Gate in a valley where magic cannot follow, performing rituals she half-believes in. One night her private prayer — spoken aloud for the first time in years — is answered by a voice. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the impossible has happened, and no one left alive can tell her what it means.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Yesterday
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A stranger walks out of the mist wearing clothes from a country that isn't on any map: Wendell, last memory-keeper of Vessany, who survived its unmaking by carrying every memory of it inside his head. He claims the gods are waking because he is dying. The beat is wary fascination between two lonely keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Magic seeps past the gate's edge for the first time — flowers blooming out of season, a dead lamb standing up. The valley elders demand Paloma enforce the old law: strangers at the gate must be turned away or killed. She hides Wendell instead. The beat is loyalty beginning to outweigh duty.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises Thin
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He explains the mechanics of his dying: each moon turn, Vessany leaks further back through the gate, and when the thirteenth moon wanes full, the whole country returns — with its gods, its wars, and the tyrants who caused its unmaking. The beat is mounting urgency wrapped in tenderness as he teaches Paloma Vessany's songs.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Badly
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Valley folk begin receiving answers to old prayers — a widow's husband returns wrong, a child's wish for snow brings a killing frost. The returning god is answering faithfully but blindly, without the context of a hundred years. The beat is horror at mercy without judgment, seeding the theme of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Heresy
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell reveals there is a true Door — not the gate Paloma keeps, but the original threshold buried beneath the Unmade Court, which would let Vessany's people choose return or rest. But reaching it means crossing territory where Paloma's valley-law gives her no protection. The beat is a bargain struck between equals, sealed by shared risk.

chapters.title: Border of the Unmade
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The two cross into the leaking edges of Vessany: streets that exist only when remembered, citizens who are half-ghost, half-hope. Paloma discovers Wendell has been editing what he shows her — omitting how the gate-keepers of old were betrayed. The beat is trust cracking under the weight of curated truth.

chapters.title: The Truth He Carried
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Confronted, Wendell confesses: the gate-keepers weren't heroes; they helped unmake Vessany to end a god-war, and Paloma's line was complicit. His loyalty made him hide it; his love of truth undoes him now. The beat is betrayal transmuting into grief, as Paloma realizes her whole inheritance is a lie told kindly.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the Unmade Court, the waking god offers Paloma the lawful choice: seal the Door forever and save her valley, as her ancestors did. Instead she claims the keeper's authority and holds the Door open herself, becoming the living hinge so Vessany's people may choose. The beat is defiant sacrifice — justice enacted where no law reaches.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, Then Morning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As the thirteenth moon sets, some of Vessany crosses home and some chooses rest; the god, given witnesses at last, learns to answer with judgment rather than reflex. Paloma remains the Door — neither open nor shut — and Wendell, emptied of his burden, stays beside her. The beat is bittersweet peace: loyalty and truth reconciled at last.
